But after facing him, he started to see why Kent chose to be arrogant when he could have chosen to escape when he had the chance.
That alone pissed him off.
However, that wasn’t the only thing that pissed him off.
He made the second discovery after exchanging a few blows with Kent.
’He wanted to use me to test his strength.’
That thought echoed in his mind—and it was true.
Kent was making it difficult for him to even use any of his Legendary-grade skills.
He was testing just how strong he had become since Grand Elder Ruolan couldn’t help him.
This alone was plain disrespect.
That was why he was no longer holding back.
Killing Kent would give him that calm.
He chose not to give him a breather, which, unfortunately for him, didn’t do much against Kent.
He charged forward, thrusting his spear in a blur—three quick jabs aimed at Kent’s chest, shoulder, and thigh.
Kent was using all the knowledge he had absorbed from his past self and the three levels of the Sword Bridge he had cleared.
It’s safe to say he had reached a stage in close combat that many could only dream of.
He was deflecting, parrying, and dodging the spear thrusts coming in rapid succession.
Kent’s feet slid across the ground like a phantom’s.
He could feel the spear qi in the air—it was as if it had been precisely coordinated to target only his vulnerable points.
But that wasn’t what Kent was worried about.
Somehow, he could tell he had no business fighting someone who was on the same level as a Sword King.
That was just too much.
Protector Navarro is a Spear King who could easily kill him using his spear realm.
However, he hadn’t done so because he couldn’t use the Spear Realm—just like a Sword King couldn’t use the Sword Realm against someone who hadn’t formed one yet or hadn’t reached the king stage.
He can’t attack someone who doesn’t have a realm with your his own realm unless he wants the Heavenly Daos to rain their hatred upon you.
So, despite being out of his league, Kent knew this battle could be won using experience and skill—something he wasn’t lacking at the moment.
With a sudden burst of movement, Kent stepped inside the Protector’s guard, his blade humming as he slashed upward.
Navarro tilted his spear and blocked at the last moment, but the sheer force pushed him back several meters.
Dust scattered beneath his boots.
"Edge of the Night."
"Lunar Eclipse Slash."
"Thousand Blade Reflection."
Kent activated three skills at once.
Protector Navarro was drowned in darkness, blinding him completely.
Then, from straight ahead, an eye snapped open, unleashing a crescent arc that instantly split into a thousand reflections.
The rain came down on the Protector, who didn’t see it coming.
He raised his defenses, but they were shattered, allowing most of the attacks to land on his body, sending him flying nearly a mile back.
He slammed into a massive tree, destroying it completely.
However, before he could gather himself, a dark shard made of the strongest mineral stabbed at his leg—grazing it, since he managed to dodge even the one aimed at his heart.
Of course, Kent knew he would be able to dodge.
That was why he had prepared something else for the Protector, who was now beginning to sense the shift in battle.
Kent was gaining the upper hand, and while the Protector shouldn’t be struggling to defend against his skills, they were proving surprisingly dangerous.
He was getting back on his feet when his gaze landed on the thousand crescent arcs coming down at him.
He knew the battle hadn’t even entered its final phase, but he was already being forced to get serious.
"Heaven Shattering Spear." So he decided to unleash his own skill.
The clouds parted as a colossal spear appeared, locking onto Kent.
Since thousands of sword arcs were flying at him, it was only natural for Kent to face something of equal intensity.
So, Navarro poured his energy into the attack, causing the massive spear to descend.
However, instead of getting alarmed, Kent smiled.
"You shouldn’t have done that." His eyes glowed as he activated one of the seven skills he had learned during the Sword Gaze Enlightenment.

chapters.title: Chapter 461: Kent Vs Protector Navarro (2)
paragraphs: One of the skills Kent learned during his enlightenment was the Dimensional Reflection Slash.
It allows him to reflect attacks back at the attacker.
However, there is a catch.
The skill depends on two things.
The first is the grade of the skill used by the attacker. If the grade of that skill is lower than Kent’s, then it can be reflected.
However, if it’s higher than Kent’s skill grade, he wouldn’t even be able to activate the skill, for he would simply know.
But it’s more complicated than that. This is where the second factor comes in.
Aside from the skill grade, the second factor is the attack power behind the skill.
Kent has high attack power, which makes even an Earth-grade skill dangerous in his arsenal. The logic is simple: the higher the attack power, the perilous the skill.
So, in this case, if the attack power behind the opponent’s skill is greater than his, then regardless of the skill grade, he wouldn’t be able to reflect it back to the attacker.
However, who is Kent?
He has broken a limit that was placed on him and entered a new phase of evolution, where he can continue growing stronger without even levelling up.

This means that while he may not yet have the body to unleash an attack using all his power, when one comes against him, he can simply reflect it because the dimensional reflection Slash skill doesn’t depend on body power but innate attack power.
His crescent arcs were raining down on Protector Navarro, who didn’t know he had called doom upon himself when he unleashed his skill out of frustration.
The giant spear appeared and descended on Kent.
However, just when it was within a meter of him, the lock it had on Kent vanished—then it appeared again in the clouds, locking onto Protector Navarro.
"What..." the alarmed protector muttered as he felt his own skill target him.

"Have you ever heard the phrase ’Back to sender’?" Kent laughed, unleashing another set of 450 sword arcs and multiplying them using the Thousand Blade Reflection, causing it to become more than 4000 sword arcs.
Boom.
Kent’s attack and the giant spear descended on Protector Navarro, sending him flying.
A deep cut appeared on his chest, showing just how much he had taken on. Kent, of course, didn’t give him a breather.
He lunged forward, aiming another attack at his eye.
However, just when he was a few steps from Protector Navarro, his sixth sense rang out, causing him to stop right when a dangerous dark spear erupted from the ground.
Kent couldn’t evade it in time, and it was too late to return it to the sender. He tried his best to dodge, causing the spear to graze his arm.
⟦Urgent: You have been poisoned⟧
A notification appeared in Kent’s vision, confirming what he was already feeling inside. He could feel the poison entering his body, threatening to boil him from within.
However, he simply used the [Rule Breaker] skill, cutting off the effect of the poison. It was as if he hadn’t been poisoned at all.
Naturally, this also meant that even if he were to drink poison again, for the next 24 hours, he wouldn’t be affected.
But that was just one effect of the skill Protector Navarro had used.
Kent had to move back several steps just to evade all the spears that started shooting from the ground. The kingdom protector seemed humiliated and furious at what the sneaky Kent was doing to him.
Kent was moving back quickly as he kept evading the dozens of spears coming at him from the ground.
However, the moment he moved back, Protector Navarro had the chance to recover, allowing him to get back into the battle.
But, of course, that would depend on whether or not he could hurt the sneaky Kent, who just wouldn’t allow himself to be caught at a disadvantage.
It’s quite shocking, in fact. Kent isn’t giving Protector Navarro face at all.
Far from the battlefield, Sword King Shawn and two others are watching the battle with shocked expressions. The two with him are elders from the Light Sword Sect—Elder Matin and Elder Dan.
"Sect Master, just how is this possible?" Elder Dan, a rather handsome fellow with short dark hair, asked. He looks like someone who has a good head on his body.
"I am as shocked as you, Dan. This isn’t what I was expecting at all," Sword King Shawn said, watching Kent exchange attacks with Protector Navarro.
"He has surpassed all of us and isn’t even a Transcendent yet. Just how can a person be this monstrous?"
The two elders behind him nodded.
"I hope you won’t be stepping down as Sect Master anytime soon, Sword King," Elder Matin asked, trying to see the way forward.
After Kent met with Sword King Shawn, the infamous swordsman of the human continent began having second thoughts about not having the means to help Kent.
He had already gained a lot from him, yet he couldn’t even help him once.

This made him start to feel guilty and useless. So, after a few internal struggles, he called his two trusted friends and elders and informed them that he would be stepping down as Sect Master of the Sword Light Sect.
This way, he could help Kent without the sect suffering in his stead. The only thing that was holding him back was the many lives he was nurturing in the sword light sect.
The moment he steps down and cuts connection with them, they wouldn’t be targeted regardless of what he does from here onwards.
However, watching now, he knew that the battle was already in Kent’s hands—with or without him.
"I will be stepping down, but I won’t sever ties with the sect like I initially planned," Sword King Shawn said, shocking the two elders.
"What..." they exclaimed. "Where would you be going?"
"Kent offered me a chance to become a Sword Emperor and finally step into the Sovereign stage. So I plan on taking it.
I will be away from the sect for years, but before leaving, I will make arrangements that won’t disrupt its flow, regardless of what happens in my absence."
"And don’t worry. Kent promised to help two people of my choosing gain the talent to become Core Formation experts one day. This is why I brought you two today.
I want you to bear witness and perhaps learn a thing or two about our benefactor"
Their jaws dropped upon hearing what their Sect Master had just said.
They dream of becoming Kingdom Protectors and are now being given that opportunity.
"Don’t look too shocked. The future of the Sword Light Sect will rest on your shoulders, so you better be prepared," Sword King Shawn said with a smile.
Elder Matin and Dan nodded.
Suddenly, a powerful boom rocked the battlefield.
Turning around, a headless body could be seen slammed to the ground. Up in the air, Veydris looked around with his bloody colossal sword still in his grip.
After surveying the area for a few seconds, he stepped back into the void, leaving behind the headless body that once belonged to a Level 8 Sovereign who had tried to sneak up on Kent.

chapters.title: Chapter 462: Kent Vs Protector Navarro (3)
paragraphs: The sword gaze Kent awakened and gained enlightenment for wasn’t as simple as he had thought. He first saw its effect during the fourth-level challenge of the sword bridge.
That was when he noticed that the more he exchanged attacks with the clone version of himself, the more adaptive he became.
It became clear to him that he could easily learn and master his opponent’s battle style, regardless of their weapon. He could learn the combat style of any weapon user.
Right now, Protector Navarro was using a spear, which caused Kent to learn and master his moves by exchanging attacks with him.
Although the battle had been going on for just eighteen minutes, Kent had already learned Navarro’s battle style and begun defending effortlessly.
But while that was shocking, it was exactly what Kent had been waiting for.
He knew that if he could adapt to Protector Navarro’s battle style, he would be able to figure out precisely what needed to be done.
So the moment he understood Protector Navarro’s combat style, he integrated it into his own. He then used two more minutes to create plans.
This made Protector Navarro sense something was amiss. However, before he could react, Kent stepped back and unleashed a sword skill.
"Void Cleave!"
A dark sword arc about fifteen meters long flashed out of his sword, cleaving through the air and distorting the space around it as it descended upon Protector Navarro.

Protector Navarro, who raised his spear and unleashed a wide arc attempting to defend against the incoming dark sword arc, felt his attack disintegrate before it could even collide with the [Void Cleave].
"Giant Spear Form!"
He quickly jammed his spear into the ground, creating a large spear between himself and the dark sword arc.
The dark sword arc slammed into the spear, destroying it as if it were made of cotton. The cut was effortless.
"Aaagghhh!"
Protector Navarro screamed as he channelled his energy into his spear and stabbed it forward, meeting the sword arc head-on.
The spear and the arc collided, resulting in an explosion that sent Protector Navarro flying. The explosion was that of fire, but tiny arcs made of sword qi and the energy of the void.
"Lunar Eclipse Slash!"

While Navarro was mid-air, Kent activated one of his sword gaze skills, calling forth a large crescent-shaped sword arc that slammed into Protector Navarro, sending him crashing down and creating a large crater where he landed.
"Worked better than I hoped."
Kent smiled as he vanished from where he stood, appearing a meter from where Protector Navarro was rising.
He unleashed another attack, forcing the kingdom protector to use a movement technique to escape, causing Kent’s strike to miss.
However, Kent wasn’t finished yet.
He activated the [Fractured Void] skill, unleashing another [Solar Eclipse Slash] from the void. This time, the attack found its mark, catching the seasoned Kingdom Protector completely off guard.
His body was slammed again into the ground, creating even more cuts.
Kent smiled.
He used the second form of the [Annihilation Sword] skill he received from Vexthra when he made Unity his second wife.
That was the only technique he asked from Vexthra.
Over the one year he spent with Vexthra before sending him to Sonox, he selected some skills he will be asking from her as he keeps growing.
The Annihilation Sword is the only skill he could wield while in the Medium world. This means he can’t use the others just yet.
Perhaps he would ask for them after becoming a Core Formation expert.
Still, the second form of the Annihilation Sword’s destructive power exceeded his expectations.
It drew strength from the Void and distance.
The attack grew stronger the farther it travelled toward its target—the longer the distance, the greater the impact.
So, once Kent mastered Protector Navarro’s moves and realised that stepping back would force the protector to shift his stance, he knew it was the perfect moment to unleash the strike.
"Too bad I can’t unleash the true form yet," Kent sighed.
Just as the first form required 450 sword arcs to reach its full potential, the second form also had a limit he couldn’t yet achieve.
But as he looked at the battered form of Protector Navarro, Kent couldn’t help but feel he had accomplished something monumental.
"I initially thought Kingdom Protectors were so great... I guess I was wrong."
Kent smiled again.
"Just who are you?" Protector Navarro asked, spitting blood from his broken jaw.
"Someone who isn’t afraid of your employers. Just tell me, why are you doing the bidding of the Hand?"
Kent asked, but a sudden, thunderous attack rocked the battlefield before the Kingdom protector could even think of an answer.
Both Kent and Protector Navarro turned toward the disturbance.
"Looks like I need a worthy opponent," Zareth, Kent’s fourth undead, said as the space cracked and a colossal serpent appeared, bringing with it a powerful presence.
It was biting into the two legs of Protector Han, who seemed to have lost consciousness.
The terrifying Zareth stood atop the serpent’s head as the serpent moved from what appeared to be a void-like realm.
In his hand was a scythe stained with blood, considering Protector Han was bleeding profusely.
"Master, you might want to end the battle soon. The weather is changing, which in Eldrich magic means a great calamity is about to befall us," Zareth said, smiling at Kent.
Kent just smirked, understanding the coded message his unruly True Undead said.
Everyone watching the battle felt their blood run cold. The sight they were witnessing made no sense at all.
The one they had all wished to see struggling was now standing with only minor injuries while his opponents were bleeding profusely.
"Just what is happening?" a figure sitting at the peak of the Sovereign stage asked, standing atop a tall mountain several miles away.
He was clad in simple armour with a hood covering his head.
"Looks like humans now have a monster, just like those on the demon, Elvin, and Dragon continents," a second figure said. The second figure is a Core Formation expert.
"Do you think they will notice him?" the first figure asked.
"That is why we are here, Zagan. We are here to eliminate all threats against our empire. We already have enough worries from those three empires; we can’t have a fourth," the second figure replied.
"Then what are we going to do?" Zagan asked.
"Just wait for now. If my information isn’t wrong, he will soon be making his way to the ancient battlefield of parting. We will have our chance then. With our power, he won’t know what hit him.
So for now, we will let him handle the threats we were also sent to deal with."
"I will listen to you, general," Zagan said with a gentle bow before drawing his bow.
"Then how about I take care of the Assassin Lady?" Zagan asked.
"Go ahead. She is injured, so this is the best time," came the reply.
In the distance, Protector Vari could be seen standing over the passed-out body of the kingdom protector of the Kyrrith Kingdom.
She was injured in multiple places.
Suddenly, she sensed her life was in danger, causing her to move back, narrowly evading a giant, sleek arrow.
However, the arrow that missed turned back and shot at her again. She was too slow to dodge this time because her left leg was hurt from previous battles.
So the arrow came stabbing toward her chest, causing her to close her eyes and embrace death, for she knew the arrow was death.

chapters.title: Chapter 463: Kent’s Warning
paragraphs: 60 seconds before Protector Vari was attacked...
"Master, you might want to end the battle soon. The weather is changing, which in Eldritch magic means a great calamity is about to befall us," Zareth said, smiling at Kent.
Looking at his first True Undead, he couldn’t help but sigh happily. All his undeads are awesome, but this one is the best.
Kent then looked at Protector Navarro.
"I am going to cut your left arm off now."
Before the Kingdom Protector could react, another version of Kent appeared behind him and swung his sword, taking off his left arm.
"Aaarrggghhh!"

A blend of pain, shame, and anger erupted from Protector Navarro’s mouth. Long before the battle began, he used the split body technique he learned from the sword bridge to split a copy of himself and waited for the right time.
He knew doing it himself would be next to impossible, considering the Kingdom Protector had proven to be a formidable opponent.
However, he lost one arm, bringing both shame and pain to him.
His right hand, wielding the spear, moved to drive it through Kent, but a voice spoke from above before he could move a muscle.
"Coil Void Drago!"
A giant dragon, about 300 meters long, appeared in the air and roared, shaking the entirety of Vastport City. Everybody felt it.
Protector Navarro, who was about to move, felt a great pressure fall on him, bringing him to his knees and cracking the ground beneath it.
"Nice one, Zareth," Kent gave his undead a thumbs-up before moving closer to the now kneeling and pale protector.
"You win, Protector Navarro. I wanted to succeed where Zareth failed, but he seemed to be better than I. So I’ll let you go today.
Of course, the next time you see me, I will be able to kill you with a snap of my fingers. I know you believe I can do that for a mere Great Sage just kicked your ass.
Imagine me becoming a Transcendent or an Ascension Stage expert. We both wouldn’t want that to happen, so take my advice and run.
If you run now, the Hand wouldn’t be able to do much to you. Who knows, we might even become friends the next time we meet."
"Clock is ticking, Master," Zareth said, making Kent raise his thumbs up acknowledging his warning.
"Become a good person, Protector Navarro. You have what it takes to transcend one day." Kent tapped his forehead, and using his soul, he placed a seal on him.
The moment he released the seal, Protector Navarro fainted, and then his body vanished. Kent stood up and looked around him
"Let this be known to all—that I, Kent Madson, your very own Swordsman Slash Alchemist—came, saw, and conquered.
I will return again, and when that happens, you all will know what real horror looks like." The words sent a chill down everyone’s spine.
"Just kidding. I will only make those who come against me or any of my allies feel the pain. Also, don’t look too shocked.
I will only be taking one Kingdom Protector today."
Kent extended his index finger, forcing a golden lightning bolt to shoot from it, piercing Protector Han’s forehead and killing him instantly.
His body vanished from the maw of the serpent Zareth was standing on and reappeared inside the Necro Forge.
In that same moment, far from Kent and Zareth, Protector Vari dodged a sudden arrow that came from her left.
However, her battle with Protector Nathan—the strongest of the four Protectors—had proven to be a dangerous one.
Thankfully, she won.
But her left leg was broken and poisoned, making her lose her balance when the arrow returned, stabbing toward her heart.
Knowing she was on her last leg, she closed her eyes as she waited for her death.
However, just when the arrow was a few inches from her, a small dark hole opened on her chest, swallowing the arrow.
Then, from thin air, Veydris appeared, looking toward the direction the arrow came from. Protector Vari opened her eyes, realizing she was still alive.
Of course, when her eyes landed on the metallic knight, she knew Kent had come to her rescue. Knowing this, she surrendered to her fatigue and fell back.
However, before she could hit the floor, Veydris appeared behind her and caught her. Strangely, his metallic knight armor vanished, leaving only a metallic yet leather-like armor around his body.
His height was also reduced, taking the form of an adult human.
The moment he caught her, they vanished into the tower, appearing in the Harem Tower, where the ladies quickly surrounded her and took her from Veydris, who vanished back to the Realm World.
Lilian quickly used her ice element to cast a few healing spells, healing herself.
The Peak Sovereign, who fired the arrow, became alarmed when his attack was neutralized. That was a call for concern.
"We need to leave now," the Core Formation expert who was with Zagan said, grabbing his hand. He knew the situation had suddenly changed, so they must run.
"Oh, but you first have to hear what my master wants to say." Zareth appeared in the air, with the Coil Void Dragon and the Serpent hovering behind him.
His hands were behind his back, yet the pressure falling down on the two made Zagan start bleeding from his nose.
"Dark Elves. How interesting," Kent said, walking toward them with his hands in his pockets.
"Are you two here to spy on me or the entire continent?" Kent asked, stopping a meter away from them.
This distance was intentional—just enough so he could escape if needed, considering the Core Formation expert with Zagan was far more powerful than Protector Navarro.
The only reason Zareth had managed to trap him was because he was using the power of the Coiled Void Dragon and the Alabaster Poison Serpent.
And yes, the two creatures are real, not made using spiritual or abyssal energy. They also, from the look of things, are at the core formation stage.
Kent didn’t know where they came from, but after the battle, he sure would learn more about them.
So, Kent was keeping his distance just in case. He could tell the general was already gathering energy behind him to attack.
"Don’t be alarmed. I don’t plan on attacking you just yet. You’re part of the Hand, so send my message to them."
The two became visibly shocked when they heard him. They said nothing, as no one except the organisation’s top leaders knew their identities. Hearing Kent identify them was a shock.
"No need to look shocked. I know you are Zagan Ty Derius, and you are General Kaelreth Darksoul."
First, they were alarmed—now, they were afraid of the youngster smiling at them.
If only they knew all Kent had to do was stare at them, and their details would appear before him like a report. The enchanted eye isn’t without its perks.
Kent can easily know anything he wants, provided he is willing to know. So, looking at him with a shocked expression isn’t something he cares too much about.
"I know a whole lot about you two to the extend I knew you cheated on your wife with your big brothers wife" Kent smile.
"You are one nasty fellow, Zagan"
Sometimes, the enchanted eye can reveal more than he wanted to know.

chapters.title: Chapter 464: Tell Them To Hurry
paragraphs: Since they began operating in this world, the Hand prided itself on being hidden from everyone’s sight for all these years.
Their members hardly know each other. Only the high-ranking members are privileged to know who is part of their organisation.
So, for them to have their identity exposed like that is very concerning, yet disappointing.
"I don’t have much time, so listen to my message well.
Tell your leader that I, Kent Madson, said he or she should hurry up and gather all the Keys of the Apocalypse and open the Gate of the Apocalypse.
I don’t have much patience, you see. And while I would love to hunt the keys down and do it myself, having pawns like you do the work will be much easier.
So tell him or her to hurry up and get it done. If you ignore one word of what I said, Zagan’s soul will be incinerated.
That will be all. Now run along," Zareth snapped his fingers.
The space around the tower had become malleable, and it stretched. Then, like an arrow shot from a bow, they were flung into the distance, landing heavily on the ground.
They ran off with their tails between their legs when they regained their balance.
"That was satisfying," Zareth said, moving back down. He stopped beside Kent, feeling accomplished and happy for having such a good fight right when he was created.

They turned to the right, watching Vaelros holding three Sovereigns with his chains. On the other side, dark strings emerged from Sylara’s back, piercing through the chests of the four Sovereigns she killed.
"They sure know how to leave an impression," Kent muttered, watching the unsettling sight that everyone could see.
Seven Sovereigns were dead, and their bodies now hung on chains and strings.
That is not a sight one can easily forget.
Kaizo, however, was standing atop two dead Sovereigns.
Kent waved his hand, and the bodies with him vanished, making the brute fall on his butt laughing. Unlike Vaelros and Sylara, he doesn’t drink blood.
Perhaps he will consume bones from powerful dead beings since he needs things like that. But aside from that, he is just Kaizo, the undead, who is never satisfied after every battle.
Veydris was back in his knight form, looking down at the three teammates with empty eyes.

"You three should go back. I will be back soon." Kaizo, Sylara, and Vaelros vanished back into the tower, while Kent—along with Zareth, who had now put away the dragon and serpent—and Veydris moved toward Sword King Shawn’s direction.
"Did you enjoy the show, Sword King Shawn?" Kent asked, smiling at the Sword King, who was blown away by the sheer brutality he and his two elders had just witnessed.
"It was indeed something," he replied, making Kent smile.
"I had to make things plain and clear to everyone before they got any funny ideas."
"Well, I can boldly say the message was received loud and clear," Sword King laughed before turning to the two beside him.
"I want to introduce the two. This is Elder Dan—he is a Sword Sage. And this is Elder Martin, who is also a Sword Sage.
They are the two I will be leaving the sect to."
Kent nodded and extended his hand, shaking theirs. "Nice meeting you two. I am Kent, as you all know, and these two are my able subordinates.
He is Zareth, and he is Veydris. He doesn’t talk."
Kent smiled, and while he didn’t notice it, Veydris turned slightly and stared at his neck... lol.
"I will be going away for at least a month. Take this and use the contents inside to handle the affairs of your sect. I will come pick you up a month from today."
Kent handed a pouch to Sword King Shawn with steady hands.
This was a chance for his Sword Light Sect to skyrocket and become one of the most powerful sword sects in the world.
"Then I will be leaving now. See you in a month’s time, Sword King Shawn." Kent and his two subordinates vanished.
Kent appeared in the tower city, where he quickly freshened up and rested for a day. When he woke up, all injuries were healed and his strength was back to its peak.
He then moved toward the mountain garden where Elaine and her parents were spending the morning. It had been a couple of days since the reunion, so they were spending time together.
The moment he arrived, the three stood up and stared at him.
"No need to be alarmed. I am Kent, the person who brought you three here," Kent said with a smile, walking toward them.
"Thank you for saving us, but where is this place?" Looking at the environment, they all knew they were no longer in Sonox.

"This is my personal domain, where everything is under my command. No harm will come to you here, and considering your daughter has just become my servant for the next ten years, you’ll be living here for a while."
Elaine sighed, hearing Kent’s words.
When she made the bet, she never expected to enter this new world. But now, she was indeed Kent’s servant; as such, she must serve him for ten years.
"Don’t worry. The time here is twenty-four times faster than on the outside, so spend a few months here. If you don’t like it, I’ll send you back to Sonox."
Kent turned to Elaine. "My capable assistant will come here in a few days to help you set up a herb farm, since you won’t be performing alchemy for a while."
Kent laughed before turning to leave. After taking a few steps, he stopped and turned his head to the side...
"By the way, your master is dead."
Saying that, he vanished from the mountain garden and appeared inside the Harem Tower. He appeared in the garden where the ladies were chatting.
"How is Big Sister?" Kent asked the moment he appeared in the garden.
The ladies turned when his voice entered the garden. He was aware that Protector Vari was hurt during the battle, so he asked that first.
"She is resting," Selene answered.
"Great." Kent smiled, turning to Lady Lani. She was now inside the tower, and there was no going back for her.

"You like the treatment yet?" he asked, causing the beautiful assassin to smile. She was initially taken aback when she arrived in the tower, but now, she had started to adapt, especially when her master appeared.
"Don’t worry. Enjoy your time here for now." Kent smiled and then winked at her, "I’ll make it even better when I return."
Without even giving her a chance to blush, Kent moved and appeared inside the Sword Tower, where he retrieved the Starbound Compass and activated it, creating a portal.
Since his soul has reached the 10th Tier, he can easily activate the compass.
He took a deep sigh before walking through the created portal.
The next second, he found himself in the Domain of Hatred and Resentment.
(A/N: End of Volume II. It was a huge ride, but we managed to get where we wanted. Now, we can only see where Volume III takes us.
Volume III: Past, Present, Future.)

From my discovery, I learned something about the Night Riders and why every immortal, god, supreme, or celestial being will be after you if they find out you possess one." Vexthra said with a sigh.
Kent knew asking why wouldn’t make any difference, for Vexthra would speak anyway, but he couldn’t help himself.
"Why would they come after me?"
"That is because of what is hidden inside the 14th level of hell."
"What is hidden there?" Kent asked again.
"To understand, or before I tell you that, why don’t we talk about the captain of the Night Riders, Kael Duskbane.
He wasn’t deemed the greatest warrior ever because he was the best swordsman; it was more like his determination that gave him that title. His story started when he was just nine.
He is from a race of demons called Sun Demons. They live in a desert-like world, where the only green is about ten percent of the world.
They are not the prosperous kind of demons, but they are relentless. They are great warriors for this world. He is from a world that contains minerals that help them cultivate and grow faster.
However, a few months after Kael turned nine, his world was attacked, and everyone was slaughtered after an intense battle.
Not even a single soul was left. Neither the adults nor the children were spared.
You may ask how he escaped.
For that, the story will come to the one they once called Twilight Brand.
Kael and Vey weren’t supposed to meet, considering Vey was born 1,200 years after this tragic incident in Kael’s world.
However, on the night of the slaughter, when everyone was dying with many running to dead ends, the sun that was still just below the horizon turned dark, and from the sky, a dark portal opened.
From within the portal, a being that wasn’t supposed to be born until another 1,200 years walked out. That was the first time Kael met Vey and the first time the Night Riders were formed.

Rumor has it that the Night Riders are creatures from Ebonviel; however, the records showed that every last one of the 66 Night Riders met at one point in time, and what brought them together was their darkest hour.
Kael was rescued by Vey, who came from the future to ensure the most dedicated warrior didn’t fall. Now, I know this doesn’t make sense.
Why would a person come from the future just to rescue a child? For that, you have to ask Nara once she recovers her memories.
Kael went on to dominate the battlefield, protected billions, and even went against calamities that just shouldn’t exist.
Ask yourself, if such a person were to fall when he was nine, what would happen to the universe? What would happen to all those he saved?
Thinking about this now, do you see a link forming?

"I see. This makes sense, considering Uncle Drew said something similar now that he has started recovering his memories. However, I still don’t understand why one would go back in time to save one person," Kent muttered.
"That is a story I will come to. But hearing it from the main source will sound better." Vexthra smiles. She wants to say a lot, but she can’t, considering revealing this is already taxing.
"The Night Riders came together when the Wraith Queen was dying. But it was much more important than that. The main reason was because of something that every god would want."
"Let me guess. This thing came from the Wraith Queen," Kent said as Vexthra nodded.
"Her heart. The Heart of Darkness is what every god wanted, and as we speak, this heart is still beating in the 14th level of hell.
It contains something everybody would want to have."
"No offense, but are all gods this weird? Why would they go after someone’s heart? I mean, I like collecting dead bodies, but come on, a heart is just too much."
One could say a devil like Kent should understand them, but his shamelessness knew no bounds.
"Be serious here, Kent. Right now, the only thing stopping me from capturing and imprisoning you is that you are the love of my life.
But others won’t share the same sentiment," Vexthra sighed, watching the smiling brat who just didn’t know when to be serious.
"Why don’t you tell me why that is, and what this has to do with Uncle Drew and Nara?"
"Actually, this has something to do with you. This story I uncovered cost me 100,000 years of my life force and a large chunk of my divinity, but I had to learn something you really need to hear.
First, let me tell you why the two Night Riders are important.
First, Uncle Drew is the captain of the Night Riders, which means he holds the key to accessing the 14th level of hell.
Second, Vey is the bearer of true darkness, meaning she has the means to take whatever is hidden within this heart.
There is something hidden within the heart of the Wraith Queen, and she is the only one who can retrieve it."
Kent nodded, sensing something profound was about to be revealed.
"First, Vey went back in time to save Uncle Drew, which is classic. However, they went ahead and became a league of riders who graced the night with their green flames.
Now, tell me if I am wrong, but why would all this happen?" Vexthra asked hypothetically before a small smile appeared on her lips.

"Kent, what do you know about the 14 Primordial Celestials, or more accurately, what do you know about the 14th Primordial being that chooses not to transcend but instead chooses to sacrifice his life for this universe?"
"I am lost, Vex. You might want to help me here." Kent could sense something that he should be hearing or shouldn’t be made known by anyone.
A part of him wants her to stop, but a part wants to hear what she has to say. Naturally, she saw it in her eyes; she wanted to say it.
"Of course you are... Naturally, this is why we are here. Everything revolves around you, Kent. Or should I rather call you Chaos?"
Kent’s mind went blank when Vexthra said that name.

chapters.title: Chapter 469: Who is Chaos (2)
paragraphs: "Who is Chaos?" Kent asked.
Vexthra’s smile showed a pained yet happy expression.
When she went for the Book of Stories and Legends, the enchantress warned her of the price she would have to pay. Of course, she wanted to help Kent back then, so she never really heeded the warning.
However, after getting the pages she wanted, the price became clear.
To someone of her status, age is just a number.
But what would be a god if not their divinity?
To them, their divinity is everything, so sacrificing her divinity wasn’t easy. However, in the end, she discovered something rather grand.
She was researching night riders when she happened to come across knowledge from the primordial era. It was knowledge that would make any god go crazy.
"Chaos is the saviour of this universe. When I say he was the saviour of this world, I mean he saved this universe and everything it contains.

I can’t tell you everything, considering my divinity couldn’t handle the backlash. Of course, I have a feeling you will know everything, so for you, Chaos is the one who used his life to save the universe.
You see, during the primordial era, life was at its peak. It was the first era after the universe was formed. Powerhouses rose, and many fell.
However, when the ending came, everyone ran.
Back then, immortals, gods, and the supreme and celestial beings found a way to transcend beyond this universe, so when death came, they ran, leaving 14 celestials.
These 14 original defenders chose to stand beside their leader, the Chaos Dragon. They fought against the creatures of the unknown for many years.
However, in the end, when it came to the life of this universe and their own, they chose theirs. They abandoned the Chaos Dragon and transcended."
"Are you okay?" Kent asked, wiping the blood that came from Vexthra’s nose.
"Don’t worry. I prepared for this moment, so I will be fine."
"Are you really sure. Getting a bleeding nose from telling a story isn’t normal, Vex." Kent looked worried, but Vexthra just smiled

She wasn’t telling Kent that those who ran were the original guardians of the Doom Gates. When the creatures of the unknown came, fourteen doors were opened, and these doors were guarded by fourteen celestial beings.

However, when the danger peaked, they abandoned the universe and its last defender, who was the only thing standing between the creatures of the unknown and the few living beings who couldn’t transcend.
"When they ran, the Chaos Dragon was the last standing," Vexthra smiled.
"Now, do you remember the seven primordial Chaos relics I told you about when you first visited?" Vexthra asked.
"Yes. You said they are the fractured pieces of the soul that belonged to the Chaos Dragon," Kent answered, recalling what Vexthra had said when she saw the Starbound Compass.
"Yes. They indeed belonged to him, but their purpose wasn’t to be used as tools; instead, they were meant to help you locate the fourteen legions that once aided you in defending the universe."
"Wait, you said there were fourteen celestials, but thirteen ran. So, where did the fourteen legions come from?"
Vexthra smiled again. She was baffled when reading the records, so hearing Kent ask such a question made her even more baffled.
"The 13 celestials indeed run away from this universe, but their absence was filled by different warriors. They are known in the primordial records as the 14 Doom Legions."

"One legion was the Undead Legion led by Kaizo, the Undying Titan. The second was the Sixty-Six Riders of the Night, led by the greatest warrior of all time, Kael Duskbane. Then there was the Soul Sentinel led by Astra Sentinel.
The Fourteen Lost Knights led by Veydris, the Abyss Knight..."
The more Vexthra spoke the names, the more Kent started to feel something huge was missing in his life. Every name felt like a memory, a promise, a destiny missing.

"The legend has it that when the darkness fell over everything, the Chaos Dragon looked up and smiled, and then he ripped his soul out and made a call that transcended the boundaries of space and time.
’I call the Legion of the Fourteen, heed the call of the Master, and take up arms.’
He shattered his soul; from what was recorded, it shattered into fourteen pieces and then seven.
From the fourteen shards, fourteen portals formed, and from within came the legions who arrived from all over time, answering the call of the one who stood tall when the heavens came crumbling down."
Cough Cough
Vexthra coughed blood, but she smiled, showing her bloodstained teeth.
"The seven shards travelled through time and fell in places where they would wait for their owner to find them.
One of these shards created a Wraith Queen who was meant to bestow the power of darkness to the sixty-six generals who once fought to save the universe.
Then, when that was over, her heart, which is a piece of the shattered soul of the Chaos Dragon, was buried at the fourteenth level of hell.
Uncle Drew is the only one who can open the gate of the fourteenth level of hell, and Nara is the only one who can unseal the heart and retrieve the Shard of Knowledge.
This shard contains knowledge on how we can transcend and enter the celestial Universe. Like every other world, it has limits, and that is the celestial stage.

However, inside the shard of the knowledge is the way to transcend this limit, and it is a way if you are discovered to have Night Riders in your legion, gods will come after you and they won’t stop until they find the shard of knowledge."
Kent took a deep sigh and then wiped the blood off Vexthra’s mouth and nose.
"You shouldn’t have paid this much just to tell me this. But thank you for telling me. I now know my existence is much more special than I thought.
For now, sleep."
Vexthra was a god, but when Kent spoke just now, she obeyed, closing her eyes instantly. A few minutes after she fell asleep, Dori appeared.
"Are you sure, Master? Those are her memories of you when you were known as Chaos. She cherishes them, so locking them is like taking something big from her."
"I know that, Dori, but look at her. The longer she remembers this, the more toll it will have on her. I can’t watch her suffer, so for now, lock her memories."
"Okay, Master."
Dori was reluctant but obeyed and locked the memories of what Vexthra had learned about Kent’s past. When she was done, she vanished back into the tower.
Kent took a big sigh.
⟪You do know locking her memories wouldn’t be enough, right? I calculated she will lose her divinity within the next seven years.
She has committed a grave karma by telling you about your past, and as such, she will have to pay the price.⟫
A familiar voice entered Kent’s head. The enchantress, who gave him the Enchanted Book and allowed him to awaken the Eye of Enchantment, spoke into his head.
"How can I help her?" Kent asked with a deep sigh.

chapters.title: Chapter 470: The Second Wish
paragraphs: The price paid for such knowledge wasn’t one even Vexthra knew how deep it went.
Of course, the enchantress knew that, and that was why she didn’t say much. If she did, she would have paid a price worth her life. Just warning her made her pay a huge price.
So she kept quiet, knowing that although the price was huge, she wouldn’t die. Unlike her, who doesn’t have a heart, Vexthra does, and that was why she knew she wouldn’t die instantly.
Of course, the fix wasn’t something she knew, but based on her calculations, she would live.
Just knowing about the Night Riders wouldn’t kill her. She was only suppose to sacrifice 100,000 years of her life span and a small portion of her divinity.
But she was wrong, which became clear when Vexthra was done reading the pages. Of course, it could have ended there, but Vexthra wanted to tell Kent despite her warning.
Now, she is losing her divinity, and if care is not taken, she willn’t be able to recover from it. But then again, Vexthra probably wouldn’t regret that.
She knew just how important the Night Riders are to Kent, so she wouldn’t hold back such a discovery despite the price...
"Do you have a way to save her?" he asked.
⟪Personally, I don’t have a way to save her, but you do. The Karma on her is huge and can’t easily be taken off her, so the best way is to wish it.⟫
"I see. For a minute, I forgot about your wishes," Kent smiled. "In that case, I wish..."
⟪Wait. Before you waste your wish, know that Karma cannot be wished away. Karma is like a limb attached to her; taking it off will leave a mark.
This means it can only be replaced. Now, I don’t know if you understand what I am trying to say, but you can’t wish away Karma.

It must take something of equal value. Now, I don’t know what you want to put in its stead, but you can wish for a way to save her instead of wasting it by wishing for her Karma to be taken off or forgiven.⟫
Kent laughed.
"A way to save her. Even you yourself don’t think that is possible, I am a mere brat, but I know when something divine is at work.

Vex is a god, which means wishing for a way to save her wouldn’t be simple. Now, I don’t know about you, but I value my wives, and under no circumstances would I bet their lives on a maybe or possibility.
If I can’t easily kill a Core Formation expert, then how much am I going to stand against a solution to fix the Karmic retribution on my goddess wife?
You said, ’She has less than a decade to lose her divinity.’ This means I have that long to save her from losing her divinity.
But we both know it would stop there. So, wishing for a way to save a god is not one I can easily handle. What if I can’t handle the solution just like how I can’t manage your quest just yet?.
I’m so sorry if I don’t take your suggestion."
Kent laughed, but a pained expression could be seen in his eyes. It was like a part of him was angry, yet the caring part couldn’t help but think of the best wish.
Thankfully, his brain is still working, and his angry side couldn’t trump his love for his wife. So he formed a wish and spoke it.
"For my second wish, I wish to exchange her Karmic retribution with my good Karma." There was no hesitation in his tone. This wasn’t because he wanted to be the hero.
No. Kent may be a brat, but he is intelligent.
Vexthra told him he once saved the entire universe. Now, if that isn’t something to bless him with great Karma, then he was ripped off.
He knew his Karma, if still remembered, should be able to handle this. However, he wasn’t betting everything on just that.
Naturally, he was betting that divinity doesn’t affect those below the Spirit Lord stage. This means even if his wish worked, the chances of him paying now would be next to zero.
He learned from Gaia way back that divinity can be sensed from the spirit lord stage, so logically, he shouldn’t be expected to pay just yet, considering he hadn’t formed his spirit core.
As expected, when he made the wish, the enchantress seated in her temple smiled. But it wasn’t just her; the lady sitting at the core of the Universe smiled.
"A nice move there, Chaos, but you will pay for it sooner rather than later. While you are Karma’s favourite, this Karma cannot be deducted from your account, so you will pay it in another way.
Enjoy your peaceful moments; who knows when Karma will come knocking?"
Her proud smile held many affections.
Kent had just bet his life for that of a god. That wasn’t something even gods would think of doing. Of course, she would have intervened if things hadn’t gone as planned.
But she knew Karma would never affect Kent. For someone who once used his life to save an entire universe, Karma wouldn’t want to come near him.
But that doesn’t mean he can cheat the system and help those closer to him. Since his unlimited Karma cannot affect him, he would have to work for the Karma of others.
Imagine he found out Karma doesn’t affect him.
Wouldn’t he offer to take the Karma of others? When that happens, everything will go bad quickly, so he isn’t exempt when it comes to dealing with the Karma of others.
⟪Looks like your second wish was a success. However, be warned, when he calls, don’t turn a deaf ear to him. Karma gets what he is after, regardless of who you are to him or this universe.⟫
"I will keep that in mind." Kent smiled, watching the sleeping body of the goddess in his arms.

If she did, she would have paid a price worth her life.
Just warning her made her pay a huge price.
So she kept quiet, knowing that although the price was huge, she wouldn’t die.
Unlike her, who doesn’t have a heart, Vexthra does, and that was why she knew she wouldn’t die instantly.
Of course, the fix wasn’t something she knew, but based on her calculations, she would live.
Just knowing about the Night Riders wouldn’t kill her.

Kent laughed, but a pained expression could be seen in his eyes.

So he formed a wish and spoke it.

This wasn’t because he wanted to be the hero.
No.

Vexthra told him he once saved the entire universe.

This means even if his wish worked, the chances of him paying now would be next to zero.

chapters.title: Chapter 471: The Best Husband
paragraphs: Vexthra woke up a day later feeling refreshed and more energetic than she could have sworn she felt the day before.
However, the moment she woke up, she sensed something was wrong.
"No need to look confused. I had Dori lock your memories of the knowledge you obtained about me and the Night Riders," Kent said, looking at her angrily.
"Oh..." Vexthra muttered, already sensing Kent was angry.
"I know you are angry, but—"
"But what? You clearly knew the price for learning something this dangerous, yet you did it. How can you be this careless, Vex?" Kent asked.
"I just..." She bowed her head, feeling the anger in Kent’s voice.
"I know you just want to help me. But how are you helping me if it means you lose your life? Or do you want to die?"
"No."
"Then why would you do something this dangerous? You are a goddess; you are supposed to know better than we mortals, so how can you be this reckless?"
"I just don’t want to be useless to you, okay? All I can do is ask about your everyday life while I stay here and do nothing.
While my sisters are out there helping you, I was stuck here doing nothing." Tears started coming from her eyes.
"I just wanted to help. I never expected to bring more problems than solutions. I am sorry." She broke down on his arm, sobbing like a little child.
Sensing her emotion and perhaps reflecting on his tone earlier, Kent knew he could have been more considerate with his words.

He spoke out of anger, and now, he regrets seeing his goddess sobbing on his arm. Under normal circumstances, he would have been shameless about that, but he genuinely felt bad speaking to her that way.
Being a goddess means she can’t descend casually to the lower realms. This frustrates her when she hears Kent fighting against one powerhouse after another.

Before becoming a goddess, she was a great warrior. She was a powerful soul weapon refiner, so getting stuck in the same place and not having the means to join her sisters on the battlefield was taking a toll on her.
Initially, she thought she could handle it, but now, she wished she had the means to fight beside them.
She wants to be more involved in his life, so when she saw a chance to help him, she took it. Too bad the outcome wasn’t the best.
Learning more about the Night Riders was her way of helping Kent understand his subordinates better and how best to protect and assist them.
She never expected to uncover such buried knowledge that wasn’t supposed to be spoken of ever.
Now, she had brought more danger to her man, and despite feeling her life force and divinity restored, she could tell Kent must have paid a huge price to save her.
Vexthra clenched her fists tightly, her nails digging into her palms as guilt gnawed at her heart.
She didn’t dare meet Kent’s gaze, afraid of what she might see reflected in those eyes that had always looked at her with such warmth.
"I’m sorry," she whispered again, her voice barely audible.
Kent sighed, running a hand through her hair. The anger that once sharpened his words had dulled into something heavier—worry, fear, and the overwhelming burden of protecting those he cared about.

"You’re not the one who should be apologizing," he said after a moment. "I should have looked for a way to connect you physically to your sisters. But I promise you will be more in my life from now on.
I even found a way to make you spend time with me outside the tower."
The crying goddess looked into Kent’s eyes to determine whether he was speaking the truth or just playing with her.
"No need to look at me like that. If I found my way to the god realm, what makes you think I can’t help you roam the medium and high worlds?"
Kent smiled, wiping the tears still coming from her eyes.
At the moment, the dignified goddess was nowhere to be seen.
Instead, an emotional goddess was in her stead, making the moment both unbelievable yet extremely intimate to the brat whose brain worked differently.
"However, before we talk about that, know that until I say otherwise, you are not to recklessly go looking for forbidden knowledge about things that concern my life and that of your sisters.
It wasn’t until your incident that I realized my life isn’t simple. So from now onwards, you will listen to whatever I say and do what I say.
If you do otherwise, better be sure to receive some spanking."
Vexthra giggled, hearing what he said.
But while she was smiling, she knew Kent was serious, so she also took his words to heart. She wouldn’t want to cause any more trouble for her man.
"And don’t worry, your memories won’t remain locked for long. I will look for a way to unlock them."
"Actually, you don’t have to worry about that. I have somebody I can ask for help," Vexthra said with a smile.
"Sorry, but even your mom doesn’t have a way," Kent said, smiling, making Vexthra squint her eyes.
"What, you think I wouldn’t know the enchantress is your mother? While she is not your biological mother, I know a lot about how she cares about you.
It was also the reason why I know she doesn’t want to see you hurt. Actually, she was the one who helped me help you, so don’t worry, Mother-in-law is already on my speed dial."
Vexthra smirked.
"I will find a way to help you unlock them safely this time," Kent said, taking her hand.
"For now, you have to wear this," Kent said, retrieving a ring from his space ring.
"Oh, are you proposing to me? If yes, then shouldn’t you go down on one knee?" Vexthra smiled.
"Girl, just take the ring. It will allow you to spend three days a month outside the tower. This means you can spend three days with me and your sisters outside this realm and the tower every month."
Kent placed the ring on her index finger, making the goddess smile, and then kissed her man.
Kent just smiled at her antics and chose to indulge her.
If only she knew Kent had to spend all his tower points just to get her this ring, she would probably be crying for him now.
But what is love if not making sacrifices like that?
"You are the best husband a goddess could ask for," Vexthra said.
"It’s good you know that," Kent laughed.
"We still have time until you leave, so why don’t we make the best out of it?" Vexthra proposed, and the dragon nodded.
Thus, for the next couple of hours, they remained in each other’s arms, having the best sex of their lives.
Kent knew the moment he went back, the ladies would be all over him. Then he had missions to complete and even awakened a few True Names.
Five continents also await him to explore and dominate while picking beauties like flowers along the way.
It’s safe to say his life was about to get more interesting yet chaotic.
Meanwhile, General Kaelreth had just reached the headquarters of the Hand to deliver Kent’s message...

chapters.title: Chapter 472: The Hand
paragraphs: The Black Sea is the largest body of water in the world.
It spans all six continents: the Human, Elf, Dragon, Demon, Dwarven, and Beast Empires.

It is what separates the six continents, making them difficult to reach. The simplest way to reach the other continents is through the Ancient Battlefield of Parting, which is situated at the center of the six continents.
So one can see how vast the Black Sea is.
However, the idea that it is the largest and perhaps the seventh continent cannot be ignored.
This claim has been validated many times when many saw the terror of the Black Sea. They said it contained some of the greatest horrors of this world.
So in some ways, one can say the strongest, most dangerous, and biggest continent in the world of Sonox is the Black Sea.
So knowing this, Nobody would expect or suspect the idea of building a headquarters in the middle of such a sea.
However, General Kaelreth, the same general who was scared off after Kent killed the attackers from the four kingdoms and gave his message, was traveling in a flying boat toward this headquarters.
Zagan was not with him, probably dead, so he was alone, and from the look of panic on his face, it was safe to say he was afraid.
After traveling for three days using preplanned routes only high-ranking members of the hand knew, he arrived on a small man-made island.
From afar, one could say this island is not simple.

It has many high-level formations and a terrifying presence guarding it. In fact, at the entrance of the island, the guards who stopped General Kaelreth are Core Formation, each exuding a powerful aura.
"What is your business here, General?" one of the guards asked politely yet arrogantly. Being a guard at such a place could only be seen as pure privilege.
"I have a message for the Hand," General Kaelreth said with a hurried expression. The moment the two heard him, they hurriedly opened the gate for him to enter.
"Sorry if we kept you waiting." The two guards bowed, creating a path for General Kaelreth to pass. The moment he left, they took a big sigh and quickly closed the gate.
General Kaelreth approached a large, majestic building standing atop a small mountain. When he got to the mountain’s base, he knelt down, his forehead almost on the ground.
"This is General Kaelreth, stationed in the Athea Kingdom. I have a message for the Hand."
He wasn’t even done speaking when seven powerful beings appeared in the area, bringing their Peak Core Formation presence with them.
They each had a different mask design on their face.
A cat, a hound, a monkey, a lion, a tiger, a bat, and a Rabbit. They look weird, but their presence cannot be ignored.
Despite being at the fourth stage of the Core Formation stage, General Kaelreth felt his body being taken over by the seven.
"Speak, General," one of the seven wearing a bat mask said, commanding the general to speak. However, he willed himself and chose not to utter a single word regarding what he was there to say.
Instead, he made them aware of why he was there.
"I can *cough*... I can only say the words to the Hand," he said, coughing blood.

"You choose death, then," one of the seven wearing a cat mask said, extending his hand to kill him; however, before he could unleash an attack, a terrifying yet calm energy washed over them, dispelling the energy gathered in his palm.
"Let him in." A feminine voice filled the area, making the seven immediately create a pathway for the general to pass. All wounds on his body were healed, and they even bowed their heads.
General Kaelreth, who didn’t want to be in the presence of these seven, whom he had only heard of, ran up the mountain, not looking back.
He seems more scared of the seven masked figures than the energy that just saved him.
The seven turned and looked at each other before vanishing wherever they came from.
General Kaelreth arrived at the building’s entrance and stopped. However, just as he stopped, the door opened, allowing him in.

Walking through the door, he stepped into a lush white and green garden, where soft grass blanketed the ground like a velvet carpet and delicate flowers of every hue peeked out between silver-leaved bushes.
The air was fragrant with the scent of blooming jasmine and moonflowers, carried by a gentle breeze that made the leaves whisper like a lullaby.

Hundreds of butterflies, each more vibrant than the last, danced gracefully through the air — some with wings like stained glass, others shimmering like spun gold under the soft glow of floating lanterns suspended from the branches.
He was immediately mesmerized by the beauty of the flowers that his worries, pain, and reason for being there were forgotten.
However, a few steps in, his gaze landed on a white-haired lady watering some flowers. Her hair was falling down her back, travelling down her butt...
He only saw her back, but it was enough to let him know he was in the presence of someone he could not measure up to.
"I greet the Hand," General Kaelreth said, bowing down.
"Speak," the voice was soft like silk and smooth like butter. General Kaelreth felt his voice return and his breath stabilize.
"I have a report from Vastport City." The general didn’t know how to convey Kent’s message to the lady without sounding rude.
Of course, he was prepared to die, but he would rather live past today.
So he started thinking of how best to handle this. If he sounded rude, his death would be imminent. So he started planning what to say.
"Say exactly what he said and don’t leave out any word. It is possible to speak from his perspective," the lady, however, made things easy for him.
General Kaelreth took the chance without any delay.
"Tell your leader that I, Kent Madson, said he or she should hurry up and gather all the Keys of the Apocalypse and open the Gate of the Apocalypse.
I don’t have much patience, you see. And while I would love to hunt the keys down and do it myself, having pawns like you do the work will be much easier.
So tell him or her to hurry up and get it done. If you ignore one word of what I said, Zagan’s soul will be incinerated.
That will be all. Now run along."
General Kaelreth repeated everything Kent said, leaving out no punctuation mark.
"You can leave." General Kaelreth was outside the building before he knew it. Knowing he was still alive, he left the island quickly, not looking back.
Back inside the garden, the white-haired lady stopped watering the flowers.
Instead, she was seated behind a small table, staring at the image of the brat who had just delivered his message to her with a smile on her face.
She is a beauty with perfect bone structure, pale blue eyes, and red cherry lips to die for. Naturally, her chest area just like her butt are as graceful as they can be.
"Message received, Kent Madson. Now, I wonder if you can handle what I have in store for you." Her smile vanished, replaced by a frown, as the seven masked individuals appeared.
"What are your orders, my Lady?" the monkey-faced masked figure asked.

"Let him in." A feminine voice filled the area, making the seven immediately create a pathway for the general to pass.
All wounds on his body were healed, and they even bowed their heads.
General Kaelreth, who didn’t want to be in the presence of these seven, whom he had only heard of, ran up the mountain, not looking back.
He seems more scared of the seven masked figures than the energy that just saved him.
The seven turned and looked at each other before vanishing wherever they came from.
General Kaelreth arrived at the building’s entrance and stopped.
However, just as he stopped, the door opened, allowing him in.

Walking through the door, he stepped into a lush white and green garden, where soft grass blanketed the ground like a velvet carpet and delicate flowers of every hue peeked out between silver-leaved bushes.
The air was fragrant with the scent of blooming jasmine and moonflowers, carried by a gentle breeze that made the leaves whisper like a lullaby.

Hundreds of butterflies, each more vibrant than the last, danced gracefully through the air — some with wings like stained glass, others shimmering like spun gold under the soft glow of floating lanterns suspended from the branches.
He was immediately mesmerized by the beauty of the flowers that his worries, pain, and reason for being there were forgotten.
However, a few steps in, his gaze landed on a white-haired lady watering some flowers.
Her hair was falling down her back, travelling down her butt...
He only saw her back, but it was enough to let him know he was in the presence of someone he could not measure up to.
"I greet the Hand," General Kaelreth said, bowing down.
"Speak," the voice was soft like silk and smooth like butter.
General Kaelreth felt his voice return and his breath stabilize.
"I have a report from Vastport City." The general didn’t know how to convey Kent’s message to the lady without sounding rude.
Of course, he was prepared to die, but he would rather live past today.
So he started thinking of how best to handle this.
If he sounded rude, his death would be imminent.
So he started planning what to say.
"Say exactly what he said and don’t leave out any word.
It is possible to speak from his perspective," the lady, however, made things easy for him.
General Kaelreth took the chance without any delay.
"Tell your leader that I, Kent Madson, said he or she should hurry up and gather all the Keys of the Apocalypse and open the Gate of the Apocalypse.
I don’t have much patience, you see.
And while I would love to hunt the keys down and do it myself, having pawns like you do the work will be much easier.
So tell him or her to hurry up and get it done.
If you ignore one word of what I said, Zagan’s soul will be incinerated.
That will be all.
Now run along."
General Kaelreth repeated everything Kent said, leaving out no punctuation mark.
"You can leave." General Kaelreth was outside the building before he knew it.
Knowing he was still alive, he left the island quickly, not looking back.
Back inside the garden, the white-haired lady stopped watering the flowers.
Instead, she was seated behind a small table, staring at the image of the brat who had just delivered his message to her with a smile on her face.
She is a beauty with perfect bone structure, pale blue eyes, and red cherry lips to die for.
Naturally, her chest area just like her butt are as graceful as they can be.
"Message received, Kent Madson.
Now, I wonder if you can handle what I have in store for you." Her smile vanished, replaced by a frown, as the seven masked individuals appeared.
"What are your orders, my Lady?" the monkey-faced masked figure asked.

chapters.title: Chapter 473: The Hand Made Their Move
paragraphs: The Hand, one of the most dangerous secret organisations in the world, had just been disrespected in the most shocking way.
Their enemy delivered a message to them using their own member.
That could not be allowed to stand.
The one who delivered the message knew that, and that was why he was damn afraid of the outcome. Thankfully, he was allowed to leave the island with his life.
But that didn’t mean everything was forgiven just like that.
On the contrary, they were pissed as hell.
They already knew what happened long before General Kaelreth delivered Kent’s message, so now, hearing Kent’s clear declaration of war, they most definitely wouldn’t let it slide.
"What are your orders, my lady?" the monkey-faced masked figure asked.
"He must die," the white-haired lady said in an icy tone.

"I don’t know how he knew we were after the keys. He even knew what it does and what we intend to do with it. This alone is enough to know he is not someone we can underestimate or have running around for long."
"I will go to Vastport City right away and kill him, my lady," the tiger-faced masked figure said, clenching his fist.
Though their expressions couldn’t be seen, considering they were blocking their faces with masks, their body language clearly indicated that they were furious.
All seven of them.
They were the Seven Fangs of the Hand.
All over the world, those who knew of their existence could be counted on the single hand. Nobody knew who they were, what they looked like, or even their names.
The only thing they can be known for is that they were just the culprits whenever something huge happened.
Powerful people died by their hands, and the Hand is what it is now because of them. Rumors even suggest that most kings are on their strings, controlled like puppets.
It wouldn’t be an exaggeration to say they are beings that could easily erase this world overnight.
So, for Kent to get on their timeline, it was safe to say they wouldn’t let this slide regardless of how Kent saw it.
They were not afraid of any king or queen, so Kent wasn’t someone they would be afraid of.
But there was someone they were afraid of, and it was the leader of the Hand. The lower members of the organisation called her the Hand, while the seven of them called her my lady.
Those who could rival her strength were just a few in the world. Of course, as to whether they could kill her, only the stars could tell, for she was one terrifying lady.
She was just a Level 3 Core Formation expert, yet the seven before her could not fathom her strength, regardless of how they measured it.
Her existence was one nobody could fathom.
So, regardless of their thoughts, they first asked for her permission before making any move.
"You personally going against him would be a waste. We have more important things to worry about; going after a kid isn’t one of them.

Also, I am not ready yet, so we can only let him have his way for now. But that doesn’t mean we should make his life easy. It would be best if he understood that offending us comes with a huge price," the lady said.
She looked calm on the surface, but the energy surrounding her wasn’t that calm. It was as if she wanted to rip Kent to shreds.
"We are ready to listen to your orders, my lady," the bat-masked figure said.
"Activate the Shadows. Let them hunt down every last person who ever worked for the Alderfords. They must kill them and hang their bodies upside down at the entrance of every city.
They must brand the bodies to send a clear message to him and everyone. Every last one of them must be killed.
Second, send a message to the Ocean Master. Tell him whenever Kent Madson travels across the Black Sea, they must see him as their worst enemy and should not let him pass.

Also, activate all agents in the Ancient Battlefield of Parting. Let them inform every last stronghold there that Kent Madson is in possession of the bodies of two Core Formation experts and a Domain Crystal.
Also, inform the other continents of his presence and make sure they understand he is a flight risk that cannot be entertained.
Be sure to make them understand, especially the dragons. Also, inform the Oracles. Tell them their enemy is Kent Madson. I am sure they will be happy to take him out for us.
Then feel free to inform the Dark Devil Church, too. They are mere pawns, but they have some deep roots. Tell them the one in possession of the Atomic Divine Body is Kent Madson.
Lastly, inform the Hunter.

Let her know a prey is on the loose. She is free to use any means to kill him and anyone he comes into contact with," she spoke with a straight face, but every word that came out of her mouth said it all.
She was determined to see Kent dead, and thus, she was willing to go that extra length to make Kent’s life miserable.
"My lady, what about the beings in the Dark Forest?" the hound-faced masked figure asked.
"No. Even I cannot measure their strength, so we must let them be for safety. If they sense the threat, they will make their move.
Under no circumstances should any of you interfere with those beings."
"Okay, my lady."
"That will be all. Ensure every last person I mentioned learns of Kent Madson. We can only make him popular since he wants to be popular."
The seven masked figures nodded and then vanished from the garden.
The lady poured herself a cup of tea and took a sip.

"Kent Madson. Though you are a huge variable, I cannot let you interfere in my business just yet. What I am after is more important than you can imagine, so handle the hand I’ve dealt you for now. There is more pain on the way."
She took out a token from her space ring and then channeled her energy into it.
"The variable has appeared. Ensure he dies before the gate opens." She placed the token back into her space ring and then walked away, entering her meditation chamber.
Meanwhile, far in the Demon Continent, a figure opened his eyes, radiating a presence that could easily trump the seven masked figures combined.
"Finally, I get to roam." He vanished with his sinister presence.
Kent, who knew nothing of what was happening currently, had his arms around the hips of a goddess, bouncing her on his dragon rod like there was no tomorrow.
A few hours later, his time to go back to the mortal realm had reached.
