chapters.title: Chapter 499: Before the Parting
paragraphs: The lady led them into a quiet hallway. The walls were smooth, made of polished wood. Soft lights glowed from the ceiling, casting a warm light.
Vexthra didn’t say anything this time. She just followed behind the lady and Kent beside her until they entered the room.
They reached a small room. Inside was a table, two chairs, and a large storage crystal set in the wall.
"Please wait here. It will take just a couple of minutes," the lady said, placing the golden herb box on the table.
Vexthra sat down slowly. Kent did the same and crossed his arms on his chest.
The lady bowed and left the room, closing the door behind her.
Vexthra looked at the herb box, then at Kent. "I still don’t know why I did that."
Kent smiled. "Because you’re kind."
Vexthra raised a brow. "I’m not. At least not to people I just met"
Kent laughed softly. "Well, maybe just a little. You didn’t kill me when I made my move on you."
Vexthra just smirked.
A few minutes later, the lady returned. She held a small token. It glowed with a faint gold light.
"The exchange has been approved. This is your confirmation token. The herb now belongs to you," she said, handing it to Vexthra.
She looked excited as she handed the token to her. Though the sale she had just made wasn’t truly in her name, it would be recorded, raising her status in the store to a new level.
"Please, you can rest here while we work on gathering the herbs you want. I will come and inform you after we are done." Kent nodded, and she left.
Kent then looked at the herb box. "Are you buying this for Lilian to use in tempering her body?" Kent asked.

"Yes. She is currently tempering her body using the Ice Heart Flower. That will take her ice element to a higher level, giving her more control. So I don’t want her flame to lag behind," Vexthra responded.
"It’s just too bad I made a blunder, and I can already tell it’s starting to escalate," Vexthra sighed.
"Hey, you want to know how mortals live since you’ve forgotten? I’d say you’ve already seen a part of it, and in case you are not aware, you are already kicking it." Kent laughed.
Vexthra pinched him as a blush appeared on her cheeks. Kent decided to tell her what had change since the last time she was here.
"In case you’re unaware, the highest grade of skills, techniques, or spells in this world is the Mystical grade. From what I know, only the kings are privileged to have such skills.
So, you pulling a technique that’s just a step away from becoming a Mystical grade cannot be ignored."
Kent knew she was really trying to be considerate, but what she wasn’t aware of was that the world had changed since the last time she was in it. The world she grew up in had changed.
"Looks like everything has changed now. When I was still in this world, there were even Divine grade skills, and even a few Immortal grade ones," Vexthra said with a deep sigh.

"Things are different now. After the Parting, the limit placed on all Medium Worlds took effect. So I can only assume the skills—and those who survived and were higher than the Core Formation—were forcefully ascended." Kent was just making a guess, but his guess was validated by Vexthra.
"That was indeed what happened. Whenever a world is parted, all those above the limit are forcibly ascended to a random High World.
Some unfortunate ones even find themselves in Unique Worlds, where survival is rather difficult."
"That seems unfair. They should at least let them decide, not just get thrown into a random world," Kent said, but Vexthra just smiled.
"That is how it’s designed. If your luck is good, you will appear in a world that can support your growth further.
Otherwise, you can only do your best to find one that can help you. After all, from the High Worlds onwards, you can travel to other worlds using spatial channels.
The fun starts from the High Worlds, where you can always find something interesting. It used to be interesting here, though—before the Parting, that is."
Vexthra smiled under her veil.
"Tell me how it was before the Parting," Kent asked, and Vexthra nodded.
"Before the Parting, there were seven known continents. The first was the continent for the Beast Race, which included the Dragons.

Though they don’t call themselves beasts anymore—simply because they consider themselves superior to others—back then, they were a part of the Beast Race, with the Qilin Emperor presiding over them." Vexthra paused and looked at Kent’s expression.
"Oh, come on. I wouldn’t be offended by something like that. But even if I did, you’re my woman, and I’m not a complete dragon yet, so we’re fine," Kent laughed, making Vexthra giggle as well.
"So there was the Beast Race, comprising all the different Beastkin and the Dragons.
Then came the Demon Race, which had seven demon states: the Incubus, Succubus, Flame Demon, Ice Demon, Shadow Demon, Stone Demon, and Dark Elves.
Though they are elves, the real Elven Race doesn’t welcome them, so they became one with the demons. Naturally, the demons were lucky to have them.

Then there was the Elven Race, which housed the High Elves, Normal Elves, and Half-Elves. Though later on, the Normal Elves slaughtered every last High Elf, so you won’t find them on this continent anymore.
There was the Dwarven Race, too. They were the most prosperous race in this world, even to this day. I would love to explore that continent one of these days," Vexthra said, and Kent could only nod.
"I also would like to see how luxurious the most prosperous continent in the world looks," Kent said, actually looking forward to it even more than Vexthra.
The Dwarves are known as great miners. So, since Kaizo can only grow by consuming metals, he wants to go there and try his luck.
Naturally, when it comes to money, he will never run out.
"But aside from the Dwarves, there was also the Human Race, which was one of the most powerful races back then. They had many human champions.
I wonder whether they still do and just choose to hide them. But the Human Race I knew was very powerful. I had many human friends back then."
Vexthra sighed.
"Wait, you said there were seven known continents. Who are the other two? As far as I know, only the ones you mentioned exist now. So what happened to the other two"

sentences.text: The lady led them into a quiet hallway.
The walls were smooth, made of polished wood.
Soft lights glowed from the ceiling, casting a warm light.
Vexthra didn’t say anything this time.
She just followed behind the lady and Kent beside her until they entered the room.
They reached a small room.
Inside was a table, two chairs, and a large storage crystal set in the wall.
"Please wait here.
It will take just a couple of minutes," the lady said, placing the golden herb box on the table.
Vexthra sat down slowly.
Kent did the same and crossed his arms on his chest.
The lady bowed and left the room, closing the door behind her.
Vexthra looked at the herb box, then at Kent.
"I still don’t know why I did that."
Kent smiled.
"Because you’re kind."
Vexthra raised a brow.
"I’m not.
At least not to people I just met"
Kent laughed softly.
"Well, maybe just a little.
You didn’t kill me when I made my move on you."
Vexthra just smirked.
A few minutes later, the lady returned.
She held a small token.
It glowed with a faint gold light.
"The exchange has been approved.
This is your confirmation token.
The herb now belongs to you," she said, handing it to Vexthra.
She looked excited as she handed the token to her.
Though the sale she had just made wasn’t truly in her name, it would be recorded, raising her status in the store to a new level.
"Please, you can rest here while we work on gathering the herbs you want.
I will come and inform you after we are done." Kent nodded, and she left.
Kent then looked at the herb box.
"Are you buying this for Lilian to use in tempering her body?" Kent asked.
"Yes.
She is currently tempering her body using the Ice Heart Flower.
That will take her ice element to a higher level, giving her more control.
So I don’t want her flame to lag behind," Vexthra responded.
"It’s just too bad I made a blunder, and I can already tell it’s starting to escalate," Vexthra sighed.
"Hey, you want to know how mortals live since you’ve forgotten?
I’d say you’ve already seen a part of it, and in case you are not aware, you are already kicking it." Kent laughed.
Vexthra pinched him as a blush appeared on her cheeks.
Kent decided to tell her what had change since the last time she was here.
"In case you’re unaware, the highest grade of skills, techniques, or spells in this world is the Mystical grade.
From what I know, only the kings are privileged to have such skills.
So, you pulling a technique that’s just a step away from becoming a Mystical grade cannot be ignored."
Kent knew she was really trying to be considerate, but what she wasn’t aware of was that the world had changed since the last time she was in it.
The world she grew up in had changed.
"Looks like everything has changed now.
When I was still in this world, there were even Divine grade skills, and even a few Immortal grade ones," Vexthra said with a deep sigh.
"Things are different now.
After the Parting, the limit placed on all Medium Worlds took effect.
So I can only assume the skills—and those who survived and were higher than the Core Formation—were forcefully ascended." Kent was just making a guess, but his guess was validated by Vexthra.
"That was indeed what happened.
Whenever a world is parted, all those above the limit are forcibly ascended to a random High World.
Some unfortunate ones even find themselves in Unique Worlds, where survival is rather difficult."
"That seems unfair.
They should at least let them decide, not just get thrown into a random world," Kent said, but Vexthra just smiled.
"That is how it’s designed.
If your luck is good, you will appear in a world that can support your growth further.
Otherwise, you can only do your best to find one that can help you.
After all, from the High Worlds onwards, you can travel to other worlds using spatial channels.
The fun starts from the High Worlds, where you can always find something interesting.

chapters.title: Chapter 500: The Two Hidden Races
paragraphs: After the Parting, only the Dragons, Demons, Humans, Elves, Beasts, and Dwarven race remained. Even back then, the Beasts included the Dragons, meaning there were only five.
So, for Vexthra to say there were seven, something ought to be wrong somewhere.
"Actually, even back then, there were five known continents, simply because the other two isolated themselves from the other five races," she sighed.
"The sixth race back then was the Marine Race. They are creatures of the sea. I don’t know if you are aware of this, but there is a sea in this world known as the Black Sea," Kent nodded.
He had already seen it when he battled the sect master after he and the ladies rescued Nara and Zaila.

"That is their territory. Back then, it was just a small island nobody dared to traverse. However, after the Parting, it expanded, creating a blockage that prevented other races from casually crossing to other continents.
Only a few saw or interacted with them back then, and from what they said, the Marine Race was more terrifying than anyone could ever imagine.
So we left them alone. And while I would love to say you should explore there, it would be best if you focused on your level now and built your strength first.
If they want you to explore their region, they will come to you—and trust me, you should definitely go with them. For nobody, as far as I am aware, has ever visited them."
Kent became quiet as he pondered on what he just heard. ’An entire race hidden under water and for years, it hadn’t been explored.’
He pndered. ’I most defineely would go swimming one of this days’
If only he knew the Hand had already made contact with the Sea race and even made him an enemy that would be hunted down to the end of the world.
Vexthra of course choose to continue...
"I don’t know if you remember what I told you when you told me about Li Hua’s unique body constitution." Kent nodded recalling what Vexthra told him.
I told you to take her to the Dark Region," Kent nodded again.

"Well, back then, there was a race many rumored to be Vampires, hidden in that region. Many claimed to have confirmed it, saying they are indeed Vampires. However, nobody can boldly claim it with certainty.
Still, I know there are people there, and they are all beings with great magic. I knew this when I became immortal. Back then, we immortals could travel down to the mortal realm for a brief period.
I came down for just that region. However, I found something I can’t talk about because the laws prohibit it. However, before you leave this world, you should really visit there.
You would have to enter that region to know more. But the world back then was connected, and life was rather good.
There were rivalries, but not on a scale that would cause races to clash with each other."
"Then what brought about the Parting—or what brings about Parting in most worlds?"
If the world used to have people stronger than the Core Formation stage, then why part the world and place a limit on it? That just doesn’t make any sense.
Why place a limit when the world could keep going as it was?
"The Parting isn’t something I can beat my chest and say I understand—I don’t. However, from what I know, worlds are just like us humans.
First, see the world as a mortal from your world. They are born, go through their teenage stage, and eventually become adults who, at some point, will die. It’s a cycle.
However, in the case of the world, I think when it gets to the stage where it would die, instead of dying, it would rather evolve.

Now, I don’t know why that causes war between races, but the only explanation I can give is that the world may undergo some tribulations, which causes the Parting. Of course, not all worlds are parted—not even in the high worlds.
Actually, don’t take anything I said about the Parting too seriously. For all we know, there is something much deeper going on here."
Kent remained silent for a while, letting all he had just learned sink in. The fact that a whole god didn’t know something so important meant it was meant to remain hidden from all.
A world is born, grows, and evolves. In some aspects, it becomes a High World. Some become Immortal Worlds; some even become gods and unique worlds.
That wasn’t something Kent could comprehend at his current stage, so he was a little disturbed.
"Why does it feel like something dangerous is hanging over us?" Kent asked, but Vexthra couldn’t confirm his suspicion.
"I have another question. Call me crazy, but can a world talk?" Kent asked, and Vexthra’s expression became puzzled—perhaps she was catching on to the madness Kent was thinking about.
"Kent, what are you thinking?" Vexthra asked, her brow furrowed.

"Nothing crazy. But since I want answers and I’m not getting any, I might as well ask the world and see if she or he can tell me something. I mean, wouldn’t you want to know what this Parting is all about—or perhaps what happens to the world during and after the Parting?"
"I mean..." Vexthra most definitely would want to know. So, while she knew this idea Kent was forming into a potential plan would most likely be dangerous, she couldn’t help considering it.
"Maybe we should put a pin in it here for now. Messing with the world can be a bad thing, you know.

The world is protected by the Heavenly Laws, and while you may be the universe’s favorite, you are not invincible in the face of the laws." Vexthra knew the brat was serious, so she didn’t shut him down immediately.
Kent’s personality is one of focus. Whatever he puts his mind to—no matter how long it takes—he will get it done and perhaps even go beyond.
"Fine. We can put a pin in it, but I won’t let it sleep for long." Kent smiled and then told his three assistants to start looking for a way to get it done.
"So we have a whole race in the sea that’s even more powerful than the Dragons, huh? Makes me wonder what these potential Vampires will look like—and their strength."
"I also would want to know about the Marine Race. Of course, since I can’t use my god powers in the open world, I will depend on you to help me find out." Kent nodded to her words.
"To think not even a god knows everything in this world... makes me wonder what it’s made of. Perhaps after my brief talk with the world, I’ll find out," he laughed.
Vexthra just shook her head and chose to tell Kent more about the world before the Parting. Two hours later, the lady returned with the herbs Kent ordered.
